# preamble and setup

```{r pathfinding, message=FALSE}
here::i_am("scripts/_mss/final-res.Rmd")
```

for collated viz + stats results for ntw mss

-   notes on the viz:
    -   main viz = focuses on trt type (NTW vs control), minimum temp, population
    -   supp viz = includes year and sex (if applicable)
-   notes on the stats:
    -   main stats = focuses on the NTW bugs and population, minimum temp as predictors
    - variable order does matter lol (ie `pop*minT` vs `minT*pop`). for the most part, will do models as pop first. 
    - using [this method](https://lmackerman.com/notebooks/prose_statistics.nb.html#Interaction_effect) for testing signif of effects (ie do LRTs via `anova(m1, m2)` instead of `drop1` (type ii anova/refits from dropping single terms) or `Anova()` (wald tests))
      - [read more](https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/37805/why-do-anova-and-drop1-provided-different-answers-for-glmms)
    
main results/figs:

1. survival: hatch to pupation; hatch to eclosion
2. mass: pupal mass; eclosion mass
3. development time: hatch to pupation, pupation to eclosion
4. adult lifespan (2023 vs 2025)
5. adult reproduction (2023 vs 2025)

- everything should have a supp + stats section :)
- posthoc is in a separate script.

### stats

```{r NEW main stats pup survival}
# fit models
mods <- list(
  int = glmer(is.pup ~ pop*trt.minT + (1|year),
              family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_expt),
  add = glmer(is.pup ~ pop + trt.minT + (1|year),
              family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_expt),
  no_pop = glmer(is.pup ~ trt.minT + (1|year),
                 family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_expt),
  no_minT = glmer(is.pup ~ pop + (1|year),
                  family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_expt),
  fixed = glm(is.pup ~ pop*trt.minT + year,
              family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_expt)
)

# # # test sig of effs (df, X^2, p) 
# anova(mods$int, mods$fixed)
 anova(mods$add, mods$int, test = "Chisq") # int: 2, 17.902,***

# anova(mods$no_pop, mods$add) # pop: 1, 42.646, ***
# anova(mods$no_minT, mods$add) # minT: 2, 78.428, ***

## tldr just do drop1 on the int and add models. (tho they lack the AIC/etc..)
## see: https://stats.stackexchange.com/questions/193643/likelihood-ratio-vs-score-vs-wald-test-different-p-values-which-to-use
## these refit the models and do LRT
drop1(mods$int, test = "Chisq") 
drop1(mods$add, test = "Chisq") 
# Anova(update(mods$int, 
#              contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly")), # should be list of x1 = contr, etc.
#       type = 3)

## (diff X^2 results from drop1 bc Anova does Wald tests (X^2) and not refitting model after dropping terms)
## also, cant specify test=F here.
# Anova(mods$int, type = 2)
# Anova(mods$add, type = 2)

# get effect sizes
anova(mods$int)
MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(mods$int) # get R^2
summary(mods$int) 
mods$int %>% glance()
  #tidy() %>% write_clip() 
#%>% ResToCsv("summ/surv-pup") # missing var of rand effs tho
```


```{r eval = FALSE}
# trying afex
# library(afex)

## see .rds in data/ bc this took 5 yrs to compute
m <- mixed(is.pup ~ pop*trt.minT + (1|year),
           family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_expt,
           method = "PB")

summary(m) 
## main difference from below is in the ests for FEs and their p-vals

m1 <- mixed(is.pup ~ pop*trt.minT + (1|year),
           family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_expt,
           method = "LRT",
           #check_contrasts = FALSE # see note below
           )

summary(m1) 
## by default, mixed() uses sum-to-zero contrasts -- so will get different eff size estimates vs the glmer() default (treatment contrasts)
## see: https://github.com/singmann/afex/issues/4#issuecomment-145884270
```



```{r OLD main stats pup survival, eval = FALSE}
mods <- list(
  m1 = glm(is.pup ~ year*pop*trt.minT,

anova(mods$m2, test = "Chisq") #%>% ResToCsv("dev/anova/surv-pup")
summary(mods$m2)
```

### stats

```{r NEW main stats ec survival}
# fit models
mods <- list(
  int = glmer(is.ec ~ pop*trt.minT + (1|year),
              family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_expt),
  ## singular fits
  add = glmer(is.ec ~ pop + trt.minT + (1|year),
              family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_expt),
  no_minT = glmer(is.ec ~ pop + (1|year),
              family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_expt),
  no_pop = glmer(is.ec ~ trt.minT + (1|year),
               family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_expt),
  ## glm versions
  add_F = glm(is.ec ~ pop + trt.minT + year,
              family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_expt),
  add_F2 = glm(is.ec ~ pop + trt.minT,
              family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_expt),
  int_F = glm(is.ec ~ pop*trt.minT,
              family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_expt)
)

# # test sig of effs (df, X^2, p)
anova(mods$int, mods$add) # int: 2, 2.488, 0.2882
# anova(mods$add,mods$no_minT) # minT: 2, 2.6909, 0.2604
# anova(mods$add, mods$no_pop) # pop: 1, 12.289, ***

drop1(mods$int, test = "Chisq") 
drop1(mods$add, test = "Chisq")
drop1(mods$add_F, test = "Chisq") # glm_add similar results to glmer_add

anova(mods$int, mods$int_F, mods$add_F2) 
# F2 is best, tho they are all similar. just use the glmer LOL

## comparing the additive models
summary(mods$add)
summary(mods$add_F) # similar betas to the glmer

# get effect sizes
summary(mods$int) # do on the int (instead add) bc otherwise var is actually 0 lol
# (bc of singular: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/afex/vignettes/afex_mixed_example.html#model-setup)
```

```{r OLD main stats surv to ec, eval = FALSE}
# filter df bc of including mass.pupa in the model -- m1
# will fit extra observations
df <- dfs_stats$dev_expt %>%
  filter(!is.na(mass.pupa))

mods <- list(
  m1 = glm(is.ec ~ year*pop*trt.minT,
           family = "binomial", data = df),
  m1a = glm(is.ec ~ year*pop*trt.minT + mass.pupa,
           family = "binomial", data = df)
)


drop1(mods$m1, scope = ~year + pop + trt.minT, test = "LRT")
drop1(mods$m1, test = "LRT")
drop1(mods$m1, .~., test = "LRT")

drop1(mods$m1a, test = "LRT")
# can drop the 3way...

AIC(mods$m1, mods$m1a) 
anova(mods$m1, mods$m1a, test = "Chisq")
# including mass is better, per anova + aic

#anova(mods$m1, test = "Chisq") # just year and pop matter lmao
anova(mods$m1a, test = "Chisq") # 3 way is marginally signif

# try to simplify?
mods <- list_modify(
  mods,
  m2 = glm(is.ec ~ (year + pop + trt.minT)^2 + mass.pupa,
           family = "binomial", data = df),
)

AIC(mods$m2, mods$m1a) 
anova(mods$m2, mods$m1a, test = "Chisq")
# more complex model is slightly better, per AIC

anova(mods$m1a, test = "Chisq") #%>% ResToCsv("dev/anova/surv-ec")
summary(mods$m1a)
```

```{r alt stats surv to ec}
# excluding pupal mass

mods <- list(
  m1 = glm(is.ec ~ year*pop*trt.minT,
           family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_expt)
)

drop1(mods$m1, scope = ~year + pop + trt.minT, test = "LRT")
drop1(mods$m1, .~., test = "LRT")

drop1(mods$m1, test = "LRT") # can drop the 3way...
anova(mods$m1, test = "Chisq") # 3way is ns

# 2 ways only
mods <- list_modify(
  mods,
  m2 = glm(is.ec ~ (year + pop + trt.minT)^2,
           family = "binomial", data = dfs_stats$dev_expt),
)

AIC(mods$m2, mods$m1)  # more complex is very slightly better
anova(mods$m2, mods$m1, test = "Chisq")
# tho not significantly different

anova(mods$m2, test = "Chisq") #%>% ResToCsv("dev/anova/surv-ec")
summary(mods$m2) # sth about 2024...
```

```{r}
# looking at pup mass
dfs_viz$wide %>%

            se.wmass= se(mass.wander),
            avg.pmass = mean(mass.pupa, na.rm = TRUE),
            se.pmass = se(mass.pupa)) %>% View()
```

### stats

```{r NEW main stats pup mass}
# fit models
df <- dfs_stats$dev_expt %>% filter(!is.na(sex))

mods <- list(
  int = lmer(mass.pupa ~ pop*trt.minT + sex + (1|year),
             data = df),
  int2 = lmer(mass.pupa ~ pop*trt.minT + (1|year),
             data = df)
)

## include sex? -- yes
## (variations of tests...)
#anova(mods$int2, mods$int) # sex: 1, 6.3869, *
drop1(mods$int, scope = c("sex")) # keep sex
# drop1(mods$int, scope = c("sex"), ddf = "lme4", test = "Chisq")
# drop1(mods$int, scope = c("sex", "pop:trt.minT"), test = "Chisq")

# fit full and depleted models
mods <- list_modify(
  mods,
  add = lmer(mass.pupa ~ pop + trt.minT + sex + (1|year),
             data = df),
  no_minT = lmer(mass.pupa ~ pop + sex + (1|year),
             data = df),
  no_pop = lmer(mass.pupa ~ trt.minT + sex + (1|year),
             data = df)
  # no_sex mod is just the above comparison
)

# # test sig of effs (df, X^2, p)
# anova(mods$int, mods$add) %>% write_clip() # int: 2, 8.4835, *
# drop1(mods$int, scope = c("pop:trt.minT"), test = "Chisq")
# drop1(mods$int, scope = c("pop:trt.minT"), ddf = "lme4", test = "Chisq")
# 
# anova(mods$add, mods$no_pop) # pop: 1, 126.32, ***
 anova(mods$add,mods$no_minT, test = "F") # minT: 2, 36.642, ***
# drop1(mods$add, scope = c("pop", "trt.minT", "sex"), test = "Chisq")
# drop1(mods$add, scope = c("pop", "trt.minT", "sex"), ddf = "lme4", test = "Chisq")

# drop1(mods$int, scope = c("pop:trt.minT")) 
# drop1(mods$add)
 drop1(lm(mass.pupa ~ pop*trt.minT + sex + year, data = df), 
       scope = ~ .)
# jk just use anova.lmerModLmerTest
anova(mods$int, type = 2) # F test
#Anova(mods$int, type = 2) # Wald X^2

# get effect sizes
summary(mods$int)
```

```{r OLD main stats pup mass, eval = FALSE}
mods <- list(
  m1 = lm(mass.pupa ~ year*pop*trt.minT*sex,
           data = dfs_stats$dev_expt
          )
)

anova(mods$m1) # ok to just focus on the 2 ways of trt/pop/year and main effect of sex

mods <- list_modify(
  mods,
  m2 = lm(mass.pupa ~ (year + pop + trt.minT + sex)^2,
           data = dfs_stats$dev_expt),
  m3 = lm(mass.pupa ~ (year + pop + trt.minT)^2 + sex,
           data = dfs_stats$dev_expt)
)

anova(mods$m3, mods$m2, mods$m1)
## adding model complexity doesnt do much
AIC(mods$m3, mods$m2, mods$m1)
## m3 = lowest AIC

anova(mods$m3) #%>% ResToCsv("dev/anova/mass-pup")
summary(mods$m3)
```

## dev trajectories

```{r}
# shared prep + plotting
.prepfn <- function(x){
  x %>%
    filter(!is.na(pop),
           !is.na(is.sup)) %>%
    filter(instar %in% c("wander") | grepl("\\d.*", instar)) %>%
    mutate(sup = case_when(is.na(sup) ~ 5,
                           TRUE ~ sup),
           across(c("sup", starts_with("is.")), ~ as.factor(.x))) %>%
    group_by(year, pop, trt, trt.type, trt.minT, instar, 
             is.sup, sup, .add = TRUE) %>%
    CalcDevSS() %>%
    ungroup()
}

.plotfn <- function(x){
  x %>%
    arrange(desc(pop)) %>%
    ggplot(aes(y = avg.logmass, x = avg.tt,
               col = pop, lty = pop, shape = sup
    )) +
    facet_grid(year ~ trt, labeller = labeller(trt = c(p_scales$labs_trt))
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(y = "ln[mass]", x = "days to instar",
         col = "population", lty = "population") +
    guides(lty = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1),
                              order = 1),
           col = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1),
                              order = 1),
           shape = guide_legend(override.aes = list(alpha = 1),
                                order = 3)
    ) 
}
```

```{r}
ps <- list_modify(
```

```{r}
                            # ) &
                              !is.na(jdate.5th) ~ 1, # change to & if counting sups
                            TRUE ~ 0),
         is.4th = case_when(is.na(jdate.5th) & !is.na(jdate.4th) ~ 1,
                            TRUE ~ 0),
         is.3rd = case_when(is.na(jdate.4th) #& !is.na(jdate.3rd)
                            ~ 1,
                            TRUE ~ 0)) %>%
  group_by(#year, 
           pop, trt, trt.type, trt.minT) %>%

            #died.wander = sum(is.wander),
```

```{r}
# dev to 5th vs dev to wander
ps <- list_modify(

         gr.wander = log(mass.wander)/tt.wander,
```

### stats

```{r stats eggs laid 2023}
# 2023
df <- dfs_stats$eggs %>%
  filter(year == 2023)

mods <- list(
  all_win = glmer(n.coll ~ trt.type + (1|cage), offset = log(n.f),
                  family = "poisson", data = df %>% filter(mate.type == "within")),
  expt_win = glmer(n.coll ~ trt.minT + (1|cage), offset = log(n.f),
                   family = "poisson", data = df %>% filter(mate.type == "within" & trt.type == "expt")),
  
  # does not converge if int
  all = glmer(n.coll ~ trt.minT * mate.ishs + (1|cage), offset = log(n.f),
              family = "poisson", data = df),
  all2 = glmer(n.coll ~ trt.minT + mate.ishs + (1|cage), offset = log(n.f),
              family = "poisson", data = df),
  expt_btwn = glmer(n.coll ~ trt.minT*mate.ishs + (1|cage), offset = log(n.f),
                    family = "poisson", data = df %>% filter(mate.type == "between")),
  expt_all = glmer(n.coll ~ trt.minT * mate.ishs + (1|cage), offset = log(n.f),
                   family = "poisson", data = df %>% filter(trt.type == "expt"))
)

# trt effects
drop1(mods$all_win, test = "Chisq") # no diff btwn ctrl/hs LOLOL
drop1(mods$expt_win, test = "Chisq") # no diff btwn hs groups

# sex effects
#drop1(mods$all, test = "Chisq") # int is ns
drop1(update(mods$all, ~ . - trt.minT:mate.ishs), test = "Chisq") # no eff of minT or if m/f/both/none
drop1(mods$all2, test = "Chisq")

#drop1(mods$expt_btwn, test = "Chisq") # negligible int
drop1(update(mods$expt_btwn, ~ . - trt.minT:mate.ishs), test = "Chisq") # no main effects

#drop1(mods$expt_all, test = "Chisq") # interaction is ns
drop1(update(mods$expt_all, ~ . - trt.minT:mate.ishs), test = "Chisq") # no effect of minT or hs!
```

### stats
```{r eggs hatched 2023}
# 2023
df <- dfs_stats$eggs %>%
  filter(year == 2023) %>%
  mutate(n.fail = n.coll - n.hatch) # otherwise breaks performance()

# for mods that threw singular with cage, switched to fixed (per oberpiller et al 2022 recommendations)
mods <- list(
  all_win = glmer(cbind(n.hatch, n.fail) ~ trt.type + (1|cage),
                  family = "binomial", data = df %>% filter(mate.type == "within")),
  # singular w cage, switch to fixed
  expt_win = glm(cbind(n.hatch, n.fail) ~ trt.minT,
                   family = "binomial", data = df %>% filter(mate.type == "within" & trt.type == "expt")), 
  
  # check_model() does not like these
  all = glm(cbind(n.hatch, n.fail) ~ trt.minT + mate.ishs, # still singular but bc of 426 having 0's
              family = "binomial", data = df),
  expt_btwn = glm(cbind(n.hatch, n.fail) ~ trt.minT,
                    family = "binomial", data = df %>% filter(mate.type == "between")),
  expt_all = glm(cbind(n.hatch, n.fail) ~ trt.minT * mate.ishs,
                   family = "binomial", data = df %>% filter(trt.type == "expt"))
)



# trt effects
drop1(mods$all_win, test = "Chisq") # no diff btwn ctrl/hs 
drop1(mods$expt_win, test = "Chisq") # tho minT is sig?
summary(mods$expt_win)

# sex effects
drop1(mods$all, test = "Chisq") # minT and sex are sig

drop1(mods$expt_btwn, test = "Chisq") # minT is sig

drop1(mods$expt_all, test = "Chisq") # interaction is sig
drop1(update(mods$expt_all, ~ . - trt.minT:mate.ishs), test = "Chisq") # and main effects
```
